title: Feasible Studentization for Overlap-Weighted Treatment Effects with Growing Discrete Covariates
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier incremental below the field floor: specialized same-sample studentization of an inherited estimator is not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered advance is uniform covariance estimation and same-sample studentization for the component estimator inherited from [Zeng et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.00118v3), using the variance construction already supplied by [Wang and Lindsay](https://www3.stat.sinica.edu.tw/statistica/oldpdf/A24n34.pdf).
The quantitative result supplies only a generic upper envelope, while the quadratic-boundary witness establishes failure of this exact procedure rather than an impossibility for other WATE intervals.
paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived uniform original-record feasible WATE studentization over d=o(n²), weakened cellwise interiority to aggregate conditional noise, and added a procedure-specific quadratic-boundary obstruction plus a generic quantitative coverage upper envelope. Math review passed, but field novelty failed: inherited machinery supports a specialized inference extension with no matched coverage lower bound, minimax boundary, new/adaptive estimator, efficiency theorem or full-class extension. No F stage ran and no Lean declaration, sorry audit or kernel certification was produced.
tldr: This incremental note proves feasible Gaussian calibration of the original-record, zero-nuisance overlap-risk ratio over the heterogeneous known-uniform aggregate-noise model for fixed \(\nu_0>0\) and \(d=o(n^2)\). Its observed-law domain is a strict subset of the published uniform known-mass class, itself a strict subset of the broader published model for \(d\ge2\). The classical pair/triple/four-index studentizer retains ordinary-record and collision variance. These variance orders exchange dominance near \(d=n\); the separate quadratic boundary concerns collision availability. At \(d/n^2\to\kappa>0\), an admissible mid-noise law has a positive limiting no-collision probability: the ratio tends conditionally to \(1/2\) instead of its true value zero, and the interval radius tends to zero. Thus the stated procedure cannot extend its calibration to that boundary. A quantitative coverage upper envelope is proved, while its sharp order remains open. The prospective application is a calibrated sampling benchmark for a published binary overlap-risk question.
gap: Zeng et al. provide the known-mass estimator and MSE scale. Generic quadratic CLTs, total U-statistic variance estimation and higher-order WATE intervals already exist. The remaining narrow obligation is uniform observable calibration of this exact heterogeneous, known-uniform, same-record ratio.
fill: Estimate the total score variance with its sample-size coefficients, retain the numerator--denominator covariance, and derive the original-record distribution and all totalization transfers. A quantitative question exposes how collision scarcity affects convergence to nominal coverage. Derive both variance lower bounds and clipping separation from overlap and the aggregate conditional-variance condition, without population quantities in the procedure.
